Hi Anna — thanks, and great to hear Acme is moving toward pilot. Looping in legal (Soojin), infra (Markus) and security (Priyom) to provide the detailed responses and artifacts. High level response here and we'll follow up with attachments and a proposed SCCs redline: 

- In-region processing: Redwood supports EU-only deployments. For an EU-only tenant we can ensure compute, storage, and primary backups are kept within EU regions with no cross-region replication by default.
- Backups & archives: we offer configurability — production snapshots/live backups remain in-region. Cold archives are also kept in-region for EU-only tenants unless a customer requests cross-region DR.
- Deletion & attestations: we can provide a deletion attestation for primary data and backups once deletion completes; for backups the technical deletion window depends on retention settings and the snapshot lifecycle (see Markus' note below).
- KMS: BYOK is supported with EU KMS providers (customer-managed keys in an EU tenant). We also offer Redwood-managed keys with strict access controls; we'll provide the KMS custody and rotation docs.
- Telemetry/third parties: by default our telemetry is routed to EU monitoring endpoints for EU-only deployments; any exceptions (third-party integrations) will be documented and require customer consent.

Hi Anna — providing the infra details below (technical, so leaving legal commentary to Soojin). Short version: we can operate fully in-region for your tenant; below are specifics and the deletion timing you should expect. Attaching the "redwood-inregion-deletion-attestation.pdf" which contains the operational steps we run when processing a customer deletion.

1) Backups, snapshots, and DR
- Primary backups: nightly/incremental snapshots are stored in the same EU region as the tenant and are not replicated cross-region unless the customer enables cross-region DR.
- Cold archives: we retain cold snapshots in the EU by default for EU-only deployments. We do not copy cold archives outside the EU unless explicitly configured in a DR runbook.
- Disaster recovery: if Acme requests a cross-region DR setup we will document the scope and require contractual approval.

2) Deletion process and retention windows
- Soft-delete: when an object/record is marked for deletion it enters a soft-delete phase (configurable, default 7 days) where it is immediately purged from live stores but retained in snapshot metadata to allow short rollbacks.
- Snapshot lifecycle: snapshots are immutable files; when a data item is deleted we mark future snapshots accordingly but prior snapshot files still contain the data until the snapshot expires. Snapshot expiry is governed by retention policy. Default retention = 90 days for incremental snapshots; long-term archive retention is configurable (90–730 days).
- Backup purge timing: after you request account-level deletion we run an expedited purge across active snapshots and then queue archival purges. In our standard expedited deletion SLA we aim to remove data from active backups within 30 days and from long-term archives within 90 days, subject to cryptographic key availability and any legal holds.
- Certification: once purges complete we generate an attestation with timestamps, affected object ids, and operator signatures (see attached PDF). That attestation is suitable for DPO records.

3) KMS and key custody
- BYOK: supported. Customer can provision an EU KMS (e.g., AWS KMS in eu-west-1, Google KMS in europe-westX, or Azure Key Vault in an EU region) and provide key ARN/IDs. In BYOK mode Redwood never has plaintext access to the underlying keys.
- Redwood-managed keys: if you use Redwood-managed keys they are tenant-scoped and stored in an EU KMS region; key rotation and access controls are logged to audit trails.
- Key escrow/legal access: for EU-only tenant runs we do not escrow customer keys outside the EU. Any lawful access requests are handled per contract and logged; see Soojin's note for legal safeguards.

4) Telemetry and third parties
- All core telemetry for EU tenants is ingested into EU endpoints. Third-party monitoring or analytics tools that are not EU-hosted are not enabled by default and require explicit configuration and consent.

5) Operational caveats
- Snapshots created by internal DR tests may be moved to separate DR projects — we will not perform cross-border moves without change control.
- For forensic exports or export requests we will provide data export packages in-region and can do in-region transfer to a customer-provided endpoint (SFTP/HTTPS).

I'll be available on the call Naomi scheduled; happy to go through any of the retention lifecycle diagrams in more detail.

Cheers,

Hi Anna — attaching a preliminary SCCs addendum redline (sccs-addendum-redline.docx) and a short cover note on how Redwood interprets the SCC obligations for an EU-only tenant. Key legal points summarized below: 

- Contractual measures: our standard Data Processing Addendum (DPA) incorporates SCCs where required and includes the right-to-audit, subcontractor disclosure, and a supplier security schedule. The redline contains two small carve-outs around emergency support that explicitly limit any cross-border support to metadata-only (no data access) unless customer consents.
- Technical & organizational: the attestation from Markus describes the T&O measures for backups, KMS, and access controls. We will add the attestation as an annex to the DPA.
- Lawful access: Redwood will notify customers of any lawful access requests to the extent permitted by law and where notification is not prohibited. For EU-only tenants we will escalate requests through our EU legal team and document jurisdictional requests in audit logs.
- Deletion certification: the attestation includes operator signatures and an audit trail; the DPA will include a clause allowing customers to request deletion certification for an agreed fee or as part of the enterprise support package.

Next steps we propose: 
1) Naomi / Markus to share the attestation (done) and a short retention diagram for Acme to embed in your DPIA.
2) Acme to review the SCCs addendum redline and propose any necessary redlines.
3) Schedule a 30-minute call for fine points (Naomi suggested Tuesday 09:00 CEST).
